mechanism_narrative: A low and stable federal funds rate environment compresses the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors seek yield in equities.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 7.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes a slowdown in corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE exceeds 7.0%, the S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction permits (HOUST) and consumer credit (RSAFS) indicate a contraction in household demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS does not produce negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production growth exceeds 100 (base 2017=100), it signals robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when INDPRO exceeds 100, the S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising labor force participation (PAYEMS) indicates improving economic conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS is increasing.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained annual inflation rate above 2.5% (measured by CPIAUCSL) signals that the Federal Reserve will tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL annual change exceeds 2.5%, the S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicate a tightening monetary policy cycle amid rising inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL does not produce negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a tight labor market regime (UNRATE below 5.0% and PAYEMS growth), strong job market conditions support consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE < 5.0% and PAYEMS is increasing, the S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.
